subject: Biology
source: AQA GCSE Biology 8461 specification (2016 onwards) — Y10 covered topic codes B1–B4 (Cell biology, Organisation, Infection and response, Bioenergetics) plus Required Practicals 1–6.

specPoints.specTitle: Cell structure: prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells; sub-cellular structures of plant and animal cells and their functions
Animal and plant cells: differences and shared features; specialised cell types and how their structure relates to function
Cell specialisation: sperm cells, nerve cells, muscle cells, root hair cells, xylem and phloem cells
Cell differentiation; the role of stem cells in animals and plants
Microscopy: light vs electron microscopes; magnification, resolution and the calculation of magnification (image size = actual size × magnification)
Culturing microorganisms: aseptic technique and uncontaminated cultures (HT only — calculation of bacterial population growth using exponential)
Chromosomes, the cell cycle, mitosis and the production of new cells for growth and repair
Stem cells: embryonic vs adult stem cells; therapeutic uses, ethical issues, therapeutic cloning and meristem tissue in plants
Diffusion: factors affecting rate; surface area to volume ratio and adaptations for efficient exchange
Osmosis: movement of water across partially permeable membranes; required practical investigating osmosis in plant tissue
Active transport: against a concentration gradient using energy from respiration; root hair uptake and absorption from the gut
Principles of organisation: cells form tissues, tissues form organs, organs form organ systems
The human digestive system: organs, role of digestive enzymes (amylase, protease, lipase) and bile
Enzymes: lock-and-key model; effect of temperature, pH and substrate concentration on enzyme activity (calculation of rate)
Food tests: Benedict's, iodine, biuret and ethanol emulsion tests for sugars, starch, protein and lipids
The heart and blood vessels: structure of the heart, double circulation, structure of arteries, veins and capillaries
Blood: plasma, red blood cells, white blood cells and platelets; functions of each component
Coronary heart disease and treatment of CVD: stents, statins, artificial valves and donor hearts
The lungs and breathing: alveoli structure, ventilation and gas exchange
Plant tissues, organs and systems: epidermal, palisade mesophyll, spongy mesophyll, xylem, phloem, meristem
Transpiration and translocation; factors affecting rate of transpiration; required practical investigating water uptake
Communicable diseases: viral, bacterial, fungal and protist diseases (measles, HIV, TMV, salmonella, gonorrhoea, rose black spot, malaria)
Human defence systems: skin, mucus, ciliated cells, stomach acid; role of white blood cells in phagocytosis, antibody and antitoxin production
Vaccination: how vaccines work; herd immunity; the use of antibiotics, painkillers and the development of antibiotic-resistant bacteria
Discovery and development of drugs: digitalis, aspirin, penicillin; the stages of preclinical and clinical testing
Monoclonal antibodies: production from hybridoma cells; uses in pregnancy tests, diagnosis and targeted cancer treatment (HT only — full mechanism)
Photosynthesis: word and balanced symbol equations; the chloroplast as the site of photosynthesis
Factors affecting the rate of photosynthesis: light intensity, carbon dioxide concentration, temperature, chlorophyll level; required practical investigating light intensity using pondweed
Inverse square law and light intensity (HT only — apply to photosynthesis rate)
Uses of glucose from photosynthesis: respiration, conversion to insoluble starch, production of fat or oil, production of cellulose and amino acids
Aerobic respiration: word and balanced symbol equations; sites in the cell (mitochondria); use of energy from respiration
Anaerobic respiration in muscle cells (lactic acid) and in plant and yeast cells (ethanol and CO₂); fermentation in the food and drink industry
Response to exercise: increased breathing rate, breath volume and heart rate; oxygen debt and the metabolism of lactic acid (HT only — full oxygen debt repayment mechanism)
Metabolism: the sum of all reactions in the body; key metabolic conversions (glucose → starch/cellulose; glucose + nitrate → amino acids; lipid → glycerol + fatty acids)
Required Practical 1: Use of a light microscope to observe, draw and label biological specimens including animal and plant cells
Required Practical 2: Investigate the effect of antiseptics or antibiotics on bacterial growth using agar plates and aseptic technique
Required Practical 3: Use qualitative reagents (Benedict's, iodine, biuret) to test for sugars, starch and protein in food samples
Required Practical 4: Investigate the effect of pH on the rate of reaction of amylase enzyme using iodine test for starch
Required Practical 5: Investigate osmosis in plant tissue (e.g. potato) using different concentrations of sugar/salt solutions
Required Practical 6: Investigate the effect of light intensity on the rate of photosynthesis using an aquatic organism (pondweed)
